strengths: Strong empirical results with thorough experimental validation: 44.7% SR on HM3D-OVON unseen categories outperforming larger models (Uni-NaVid, TANGO), supported by comprehensive ablations and statistical significance testing

Novel and well-motivated EALM mechanism: Elegantly solves brittle manual DAgger-PPO phase switching by automatically interpolating based on policy entropy, achieving 33% reduction in sample complexity and 10% collision reduction
Practical design for real-world deployment: Lightweight model (130M params) with RGB-only input, edge-device inference feasibility (132ms on Jetson Orin), and promised code release

Comprehensive experimental methodology: Extensive ablations isolating component contributions, entropy threshold analysis (Appendix C), failure analysis (Table 5), statistical significance testing, and real robot demonstration
Clear presentation and reproducibility: Well-organized paper with informative visualizations, complete hyperparameter specifications in appendix, and detailed training dynamics analysis
weaknesses: Critical segmentation dependency with substantial performance cliff: 69.3% SR with ground-truth masks drops to 28.8% with raw YOLOE predictions, then recovers to 44.7% only after manual per-category confidence calibration—this 24.6 percentage point gap severely limits real-world applicability

Semantic reward uses ground-truth mask area at inference time (Eq. 4), creating train-test mismatch and undermining end-to-end learning claims; auxiliary segmentation loss increases collisions (45.4 vs 29.4) without adequate investigation of this safety-performance trade-off

Limited technical novelty: Primarily combines existing components (SigLIP [38], transformer [38], DCGAN). Binary goal mask input acknowledged as prior work (PixelNav). EALM is the main novel contribution but is relatively straightforward entropy-weighted interpolation

Generalization claims overstated: 'Unseen categories' remain within HM3D simulator's visual distribution; no cross-environment (AI2-Thor, ProcTHOR) or cross-dataset evaluation. Real robot experiments limited to 2 demonstrations with different camera FoV (105° vs 42°), not true sim-to-real transfer

Two-stage training protocol deviates from end-to-end: 200M steps with ground-truth masks followed by 15M with predicted masks. Requires manual per-category threshold calibration that doesn't scale. Unclear if hyperparameters generalize beyond HM3D

Evaluation limited to single benchmark: Only HM3D-OVON assessment with no cross-benchmark validation. Insufficient real-world validation with acknowledged 'risky behavior near goal' due to reward design

EALM hyperparameter justification incomplete: Entropy bounds derived heuristically; EMA coefficient α=0.95 unjustified; sensitivity analysis limited to Appendix C only. Generalization to different action spaces unclear

Incomplete ablations: No justification for ResNet9 mask encoder vs alternatives; context length (100 steps) not ablated; Table 3 shows goal mask provides 8.4% improvement but unclear how essential other components are

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation with rigorous ablations, statistical significance testing, and detailed analysis of training dynamics across multiple strategies (PPO, DAgger, EarlySwitcher, EALM)
Strong empirical results achieving 40.1% SR on unseen categories without depth/odometry, matching or exceeding methods with additional sensors, while being lightweight (130M parameters, RGB-only)
Novel EALM mechanism provides principled smooth transition between behavior cloning and RL, eliminating brittle manual phase scheduling through entropy-based adaptive weighting
Excellent reproducibility with comprehensive hyperparameter tables, training curves, loss component analysis, and promised code release enabling replication
Practical consideration of real-world deployment by proposing adaptation strategies (mask filtering, per-category confidence calibration) for predicted segmentation from pre-trained models
Collision metric analysis reveals overfitting that success rate alone obscures, demonstrating nuanced understanding of navigation safety and generalization
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: binary mask input similar to prior work (PixelNav), auxiliary segmentation loss is well-established multi-task learning, and EALM is essentially entropy-weighted interpolation between existing losses rather than a fundamental innovation

Critical dependence on segmentation quality with 43% relative performance drop (70.4% to 40.1% SR) between ground-truth and predicted masks; Table 11 shows complete breakdown (0.1% SR) without masks, questioning practical applicability

Ad-hoc and manual adaptation strategies undermine generalization claims: per-category confidence thresholds require calibration (Figures 6-10), hardcoded pixel thresholds (32×32, 1000 pixels) lack principled justification, and manual category removal reduces scalability

Single-benchmark evaluation limits generalization claims: only HM3D-OVON tested without cross-simulator validation; 'strong generalization' refers only to unseen categories within same dataset, not new environments; no real-world validation despite deployment claims

EALM contribution is modest: marginal improvement over baselines on seen categories (42.5% vs 41.3% SR, ~3%), entropy bounds chosen without sensitivity analysis, and lack of theoretical justification for why entropy weighting outperforms alternatives

Auxiliary segmentation loss exhibits trade-off contradicting its benefit: increases SR but decreases SPL (40.8→39.4) and increases collisions (14.5→18.8 in Table 3); authors' dismissal of SPL/collision metrics as less important is somewhat arbitrary

Goal mask encoder (ResNet9, 128-dim) lacks ablation or justification; no comparison to alternative architectures; missing sensitivity analyses for critical hyperparameters (entropy bounds, mask pixel thresholds, EMA coefficient α)

Segmentation model choice (YOLOE) not validated against alternatives (SAM, DINO); confidence threshold calibration process is not reproducible without access to all per-category curves; unclear how method would perform with fundamentally different segmentation errors
